reasons: Classification is correct: Section 12(b) limits TrueLink's indemnity to its own breach/non-performance with no third-party IP infringement coverage, and there is no non-infringement warranty for a breach-based indemnity to attach to — so the clause fails the fallback (which requires a vendor IP indemnity) and sits close to walk-away territory.

The redline is actionable and directionally correct for us as Client: it adds IP infringement, breach of law, unauthorized access to Client Content, and gross negligence/willful misconduct to TrueLink's indemnity, plus a reciprocal notice/control/cooperation procedure, while leaving Client's existing indemnity untouched (no self-inflicted expansion of our obligations).

The failed 'minimal edit' check (0.852 changed-character ratio) is justified here: inserting multiple new indemnity triggers into a single-limb sentence necessarily requires restructuring it into an enumerated list; the original breach limb is preserved verbatim as clause (i).

The failed 'vendor indemnity for IP infringement present' regex is a phrasing artifact — the inserted text expressly covers allegations that the Interface, Hosting Services, Support Services or deliverables 'infringe or misappropriate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret or other intellectual property right of any third party'.

Comment is accurate, concise, in the right voice, cites the playbook position and offers the IP-only fallback with standard exclusions; minor drafting nits (no express 'defend' verb added to the operative indemnity; no 3x super-cap discussion) do not undermine the finding.
